title: Trematode infections in cattle and their vector snails in Rajshahi district in Bangladesh

institutions.name: Department of Parasitology, Faculty of Veterinary Science, Bangladesh Agricultural University
Department of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Faculty of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, University of Rajshahi

abstract: The prevalence of snail-borne trematodes (SBTs) of cattle and their vector snails in Rajshahi district in Bangladesh were determined. A total of 380 faecal samples of cattle were collected and examined using Modified Stoll's Ova Counting Technique. Of the samples examined, 130 (34.2%) animals were found affected with SBTs, and the mean egg per gram of faeces (EPG) was 180.3 ± 0.8. The trematodal infections by Fasciola gigantica (1.1%), different amphistomes (32.9%), and Schistosoma spindale (0.8%) were detected among the infected cattle.

sections.title: Introduction
content: Snail-borne trematode (SBT) infections represent a significant global constraint on livestock production, resulting in chronic wasting, decreased milk yield, and substantial economic losses in tropical agro-ecosystems.

In Bangladesh, climatic factors such as high humidity, seasonal waterlogging, and abundant aquatic vegetation favor the proliferation of intermediate freshwater snail hosts, accelerating parasite transmission among grazing cattle.

sections.title: Materials and Methods
content: A cross-sectional epidemiological study was carried out in Puthia upazila within Rajshahi district. A total of 380 fresh fecal specimens were randomly gathered from cattle across varied age groups, body condition scores, and breeds.
Parasitological processing was conducted using Modified Stoll's Ova Counting Technique to identify eggs per gram (EPG) under high-power optical microscopy.

sections.title: Results and Discussion
content: Overall prevalence of SBTs was 34.2%. Amphistomes exhibited the dominant infection rate at 32.9%, followed by Fasciola gigantica (1.1%) and Schistosoma spindale (0.8%).
Significantly higher infection rates were detected in female cattle, animals with poor body condition scores, and indigenous local breeds grazing near marshland water bodies.

sections.title: Conclusions
content: Snail-borne trematodes remain highly endemic among bovine herds in Rajshahi. Regular strategic anthelmintic therapy alongside snail control measures is imperative to minimize transmission risks.
